text:
maya: Quick sync — we need one coherent answer for SDK surfaces across Python/TS/Go: transport abstraction, retries, and pagination semantics for the 1.0 client. Can we lock down a path today?

sam: +1. what's the non-negotiable constraints?

maya: three things: 1) language idiomatic ergonomics, 2) predictable retry semantics (sane defaults + opt-out), 3) continuation tokens that avoid client-side reconstruction.

charlie: FWIW I think the transport should be a tiny adapter layer. Keep it HTTP-centric by default but pluggable for gRPC/streaming. SDKs expose a single high-level call shape and we wire transports under the hood.

liam: agree. Also: retries only for idempotent ops by default. For mutate calls we should require explicit idempotency keys. doc+SDK helpers to generate them.

oskari: For pagination: server returns opaque resume_token. SDK iterator should just yield items and expose a low-level pages() that returns {items, resume_token}. Do not let SDKs synthesize page numbers or offsets.

sam: sounds good. How do we expose this idiomatically in each lang? Example idea:
```ts
for await (const item of client.listWidgets()) {
  // item-level async iterator
}
// and paged API
for await (const page of client.listWidgets.pages({pageSize: 100})) {
  // page.items, page.resumeToken
}
```

charlie: Python: generator + .pages() returning Page objects with .items and .resume_token. Go: channel-based iterator + Pages() method returning a struct. Keep names consistent (.pages, .resume_token) across languages.

liam: Retry policy: default exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts 5. Honor Retry-After header and server-provided retry hints. Expose a RetryPolicy object users can override per-call.

maya: Important: instrumentation. Console/observability needs to see which transport and retry policy was used per-route. Add a small header X-RW-Transport and X-RW-Retry-Policy for internal tracing.

charlie: Regarding resume_token invalidation: server may invalidate tokens after model rollouts. SDK should surface a specific error type (ResumeTokenInvalid) and a helper to restart from beginning or from a bookmarked prompt.

sam: Edgecase: short-lived tokens (e.g., per-request leases). We should include TTL in the page metadata so SDK can preemptively surface a warning before retrying many times.

oskari: +1. Also fallback behavior: if SDK sees a transient transport failure for a paged list, it should retry at the page boundary not item-by-item — cheaper and predictable. Document this clearly.

liam: On streaming vs paged: streaming endpoints (server push) should be offered separately as .stream() with different retry semantics (idempotency via checkpoint tokens). Don't conflate with list pagination.

maya: Proposal summary:
- transport: tiny pluggable adapter, default HTTP.
- retries: default exp+jit, max 5, per-call override, retries only for idempotent ops unless idempotency key provided.
- pagination: opaque resume_token in page metadata, SDK exposes item-level iterator and pages(), page retries at boundary.
- streaming: separate surface with checkpoint tokens, separate retry policy.
- observability: add header hints and surface policy choice in logs.

charlie: I'll draft a short RFC snippet and an example matrix for Python/TS/Go ergonomics.

maya: Great — can you include a minimal migration plan for existing clients (we need a deprecation window for old cursor behavior)?

charlie: Yep. I'll drop a draft here by EOD.

build-bot: Reminder: please include a changelog entry when the RFC lands. :robot_face:

maya: Thanks everyone — meeting follow-up: charlie will write RFC, liam will prototype policy object, oskari will sketch pagination test harness.

sam: ack.

liam: estimated prototype in ~3d.

oskari: I'll prep test cases for resume_token expiry and server-migration scenarios.
